title: The Future of Management — Fundamentals of Management
description: This entry covers The Future of Management as part of the fundamentals of management. In this field, controlling matters because measuring results and correcting course. It is taught at the Advanced level of the teaching ladder, building from first principles toward professional practice, with each concept defined before it is used.
overview: Management is the field concerned with Getting work done through people: planning, organizing, leading, and controlling organizations. The Future of Management belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Controlling — measuring results and correcting course. And Performance management — goals, feedback, and accountability developing people. Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Advanced tier.
core_concepts: Controlling: measuring results and correcting course.
Performance management: goals, feedback, and accountability developing people.
key_laws: SMART goals: specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound objectives.
Pareto principle: the vital few inputs driving most results.
vocabulary: Delegation: assigning authority with accountability.
Escalation: raising issues beyond one's authority to resolve.
methods: Feedback: specific, timely, actionable conversations.
history: Management became a discipline with Taylor's scientific management and Fayol's functions; the Hawthorne studies added human relations. Drucker's 1954 Practice of Management professionalized it, and agile plus data have reshaped modern practice.
key_points: Controlling: measuring results and correcting course.
